questions.question: Q1(a). Determine the nature of the roots of x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0.
questions.solution: D = (-6)²-4(1)(5) = 36-20 = 16 > 0 and a perfect square. Roots real, rational, unequal: x = (6±4)/2 = 5, 1. Boxed real, rational, unequal (matches the printed key, book p357).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q1(a); book p356 = PDF p383 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: D = 16+12 = 28 > 0, not a square → irrational unequal.
questions.question: Q1(b). Determine the nature of the roots of x^2 - 4x - 3 = 0.
questions.solution: D = 16+12 = 28 > 0, not a perfect square. Boxed real, irrational, unequal (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q1(b); book p356 = PDF p383 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(c). Determine the nature of the roots of x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0.
questions.solution: D = 36-36 = 0. Roots real, rational, equal: x = 3 (double). Boxed real, rational, equal (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q1(d). Determine the nature of the roots of 4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0.
questions.solution: D = 16-16 = 0. Roots real, rational, equal: x = 4/8 = 1/2 (double). Boxed real, rational, equal (matches the printed key).

questions.question: Q1(e). Determine the nature of the roots of 2x^2 - 9x + 35 = 0.
questions.solution: D = 81-4(2)(35) = 81-280 = -199 < 0. Boxed imaginary and unequal (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q1(e); book p356 = PDF p383 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(f). Determine the nature of the roots of 4x^2 + 8x - 5 = 0.
questions.solution: D = 64+80 = 144 > 0, perfect square. Roots (-8±12)/8: 1/2, -5/2. Boxed real, rational, unequal (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q1(f); book p356 = PDF p383 (vision read)

questions.question: Q2. For what values of p will 5x^2 - px + 45 = 0 have equal roots? (HSEB 2056)
questions.solution: D = p²-900 = 0, so p² = 900. Boxed p = ±30 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q2 (HSEB 2056); book p356 = PDF p383 (vision read)

questions.question: Q3. If x^2 + 2(k + 2)x + 9k = 0 has equal roots, find k.
questions.solution: D = 4(k+2)²-36k = 4(k²+4k+4-9k) = 4(k²-5k+4) = 4(k-1)(k-4) = 0. Boxed k = 1 or 4 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q3; book p356 = PDF p383 (vision read)

questions.question: Q4. For what value of a will x^2 - (3a - 1)x + 2(a^2 - 1) = 0 have equal roots?
questions.solution: D = (3a-1)²-8(a²-1) = 9a²-6a+1-8a²+8 = a²-6a+9 = (a-3)² = 0. Boxed a = 3 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q4; book p356 = PDF p383 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5. If the roots of (a^2 + b^2)x^2 - 2(ac + bd)x + (c^2 + d^2) = 0 are equal, show that a/b = c/d.
questions.solution: D/4 = (ac+bd)²-(a²+b²)(c²+d²) = a²c²+2acbd+b²d²-a²c²-a²d²-b²c²-b²d² = -(a²d²-2acbd+b²c²) = -(ad-bc)². Equal roots ⟺ D = 0 ⟺ ad = bc ⟺ a/b = c/d (b,d ≠ 0). ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q5; book p357 = PDF p384 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: D/4 = (b²-ca)²-(a²-bc)(c²-ab) = b⁴-... = A(a³+b³+c³-3abc) with b = 0 as the other factor.
questions.question: Q6. Show the roots of (a^2 - bc)x^2 + 2(b^2 - ca)x + (c^2 - ab) = 0 are equal if b = 0 or a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc = 0.
questions.solution: D/4 = (b²-ca)²-(a²-bc)(c²-ab) = b⁴-2b²ca+c²a²-(a²c²-a³b-bc³+ab²c) = b⁴-3b²ca+a³b+bc³ = b(b³-3bca+a³+c³) = b(a³+b³+c³-3abc). D = 0 ⟺ b = 0 or a³+b³+c³-3abc = 0. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q6; book p357 = PDF p384 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: With s = a+b+c = 0: coefficient ratio (2s-3a):(2s-3b):(2s-3c) = -3a:-3b:-3c, so D = 9(b²-4... ) — actually substitute c = -a-b and check D is a non-negative square of a rational.
questions.question: Q7. If a, b, c are rational and a + b + c = 0, show the roots of (b + c - a)x^2 + (c + a - b)x + (a + b - c) = 0 are rational.
questions.solution: b+c-a = -2a, c+a-b = -2b, a+b-c = -2c (using s = 0). Equation: -2ax²-2bx-2c = 0, i.e. ax²+bx+c = 0 with c = -a-b. D = b²-4a(-a-b) = b²+4a²+4ab = (2a+b)², a perfect square of a rational. Roots (-b±(2a+b))/2a are rational. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q7; book p357 = PDF p384 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: (x-a)(x-b) = k² expands to x²-(a+b)x+ab-k² = 0 with D = (a-b)²+4k² ≥ 0 always.
questions.question: Q8. Prove the roots of (x - a)(x - b) = k^2 are real for all k.
questions.solution: x²-(a+b)x+ab-k² = 0. D = (a+b)²-4(ab-k²) = (a-b)²+4k² ≥ 0 for all real a,b,k. Hence real roots. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q8; book p357 = PDF p384 (vision read)

questions.question: Q9. Show the roots of x^2 - 4abx + (a^2 + 2b^2)^2 = 0 are imaginary.

questions.knowledgeNote: First D₁ = 4(p²-2q²) > 0 gives p² > 2q²; second D₂ = 4q²-4(p²-q²) = 8q²-4p² < 0.
questions.question: Q10. If the roots of qx^2 + 2px + 2q = 0 are real and unequal, prove the roots of (p + q)x^2 + 2qx + (p - q) = 0 are imaginary.
questions.solution: D₁ = 4p²-8q² = 4(p²-2q²) > 0, so p² > 2q². D₂ = 4q²-4(p+q)(p-q) = 4q²-4(p²-q²) = 8q²-4p² = 4(2q²-p²) < 0 (from p² > 2q²). Hence the second equation has imaginary roots. ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.12 Ex 12.1 Q10; book p357 = PDF p384 (vision read)
